source.title: Mean-Pooled Cosine Similarity is Not Length-Invariant: Theory and Cross-Domain Evidence for a Length-Invariant Alternative

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Tests whether cross-language similarity depends on the metric and input lengths, and argues that mean-pooled cosine can create a misleading privileged-pivot interpretation while length-invariant CKA still finds cross-language similarity.
record.gate_note: The study measures length-related similarity under different metrics and reports cross-language CKA values. It does not test whether alignment rises with model scale or capability, whether independently trained models converge across architectures, or whether features recur. Values cited from prior work are not recorded as results.
record.test_reason: The study compares representations of different inputs (languages, code languages, caption lengths) inside one model. It measures how mean-pooled cosine, RV and CKA respond to sequence length. It never compares representations across independently trained models, seeds or modalities, which is what every version, V6 included, is about. Its metric-dependence and cross-language CKA results concern a related but different construct: within-model cross-lingual similarity, not cross-model convergence. They are recorded under fits_no_version. The paper does not cite the original sources.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is correct. Mean-pooled cosine is not length-invariant under anisotropy, and CKA should be the default. Under CKA, cross-language convergence within models is real, but the privileged English/Python pivot reading is a metric artifact.
record.recipe_differences: Uses cross-language representation comparisons and length-regression analyses across cosine, RV, and CKA, rather than reproducing the original same-seed convergence method. It also tests synthetic vectors and cross-domain cases.
record.method_sensitivity: The observed length association varies with similarity metric (mean-pooled cosine, RV, CKA), pooling regime (EOS versus mean pooling in CLIP), domain, and model. The study attributes the CLIP difference to lower anisotropy and distinguishes the EOS context-length effect.

fits_no_version.finding: Within single models, mean-pooled cosine similarity between parallel inputs in different languages is driven by token-length ratio (R² 0.23–0.79). Linear CKA removes this dependence (R² ≤0.05) and flips the sign of the length coefficient in CodeLlama-7B.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model cross-lingual similarity measured by mean-pooled cosine is confounded by tokenization length under anisotropy; length-invariant metrics remove it.

fits_no_version.finding: Linear CKA at shared token positions between languages inside one model is high: 0.9997 in Mistral-7B (EN-FR, EN-DE) and 0.52–0.997 across four code LLMs.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multilingual and multi-language models represent parallel content in different languages similarly (within-model cross-lingual convergence).

record.problems: The authors note that the code experiments cover four models from two families; the CLIP experiment uses synthetic captions paired with a fixed random-noise image. CKA uses shared-surface-form alignment with a selection effect and at least three shared tokens, and only linear CKA is tested. The theoretical expression assumes isotropic noise and is described as approximate. No scale or capability sweep is reported.

untested.parts: No comparison of independently trained models; no scale or capability sweep.
No test of image-caption alignment between separate vision and language models; CLIP is used only with a fixed noise image.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test.
No test of recurring features or circuits.
Metric dependence is shown only for within-model cross-input similarity, not for cross-model convergence.
No cross-model alignment level, plateau, or test of its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader linked the rows to V6 and V7 and gave V7 a 'challenges' label. That conflates within-model cross-language similarity with the claim's cross-model convergence. No row compares two models, so all labels are dropped. The near-1 CKA values also rest on shared surface-form token alignment, which the authors flag as a selection effect.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep and no comparison of independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.

CLIP is tested for length effects under two pooling regimes, using synthetic captions paired with a fixed random-noise image. The study does not test whether image-caption alignment rises as vision and language models improve.
No comparison across random initializations, shared features, or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired interchangeability test.
No test of recurring interpretable features or circuits.
The study compares mean-pooled cosine, CKA, and RV and tests several domains and datasets. It does not test neighbour-count settings or out-of-distribution inputs.

It reports cross-language CKA similarity, but does not test convergence across independently trained models, whether alignment plateaus with scale, or whether shared training data or objectives cause the alignment.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Code, natural-language, and CLIP comparisons across metrics or pooling regimes
reader_labels.reason: Length associations under cosine are substantially reduced, absent, or reversed under CKA in the reported comparisons, and the CLIP result differs between EOS and mean pooling (r5–r23).

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.condition: Reported cross-language CKA measurements for the tested language pairs
reader_labels.reason: The measured CKA values are high, including 0.997–0.9997 in several conditions, rather than showing alignment far from complete in these tested settings (r26–r29).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Code-language comparisons in CodeLlama-7B and CodeLlama-7B-Python
reader_labels.reason: The reported aggregate CKA values are lower for these models (0.650 and 0.523) than for the other tested code models, so the degree of measured alignment varies by model (r24–r25).
